Conclusion

Symposium pp. 105-106
Diotima’s ascent, as Socrates reports it in the Symposium, 210a–211d:

Love of one beautiful body.
Recognition that the beauty in different bodies is related, leading to love of bodily beauty generally.
Greater concern for beauty of soul, expressed in care and conversation that help someone become better.
Beauty in practices and laws.
Beauty in branches of knowledge, widening inquiry beyond one person or practice.
Beauty itself, which Diotima describes as unchanging and independent of particular beautiful things.

The ascent changes what the lover understands and pursues. Its final object is the Form of Beauty.
